findings.oracle: Replaced smoke check with test_known_transforms_have_exact_category_and_description + test_transform_names_are_unique: the native list_transforms() output is compared field-by-field against an independent EXPECTED_TRANSFORM_REGISTRY spec (e.g. base64_encode->('encoding','Base64 encode'), bit_invert->('bitops','Bitwise NOT each byte')) and uniqueness of all names is asserted; a garbage/renamed/recategorised entry goes red.

test_every_entry_is_three_nonempty_string_fields keeps the 3-tuple/non-empty-string shape gate, and test_listed_byte_transforms_actually_execute runs each advertised name (bit_invert, byte_reverse, base64_encode) on payload 10 20 30 40 and asserts exact bytes (EF DF CF BF / 40 30 20 10 / base64.b64encode oracle), proving the names map to working transforms not bogus data.

test_listed_byte_transforms_actually_execute asserts every name returned by list_transforms() is callable via transform_data and produces the independently-known expected output on a fixed 4-byte payload (base64 via stdlib oracle, bit_invert/byte_reverse via hand-verified constants); an arbitrary-string registry would fail because the name would not execute to the expected bytes.

test_base64_encode_at_nonzero_offset uses Python stdlib base64.b64encode(sample[32:48]) as the independent oracle for the exact native output, then decodes the native result with base64.b64decode and asserts it reproduces exactly the requested input slice; both the encode-equality and decode-round-trip must hold.

test_xor_at_nonzero_offset_matches_precomputed_constant asserts mask_xor(range(16),offset=4,len=4,pattern=0xFF) == hardcoded literal FB FA F9 F8 (independently re-derived as bytes 04 05 06 07 XOR FF, not an inline copy of the production loop); offset-range correctness and XOR correctness both gated; a multibyte sibling asserts DE AC BC EC DA A8 B8 E8.

TestFileMonitorRuntime.test_self_created_file_event_is_logged_with_exact_path writes a uniquely-named file under the watched public-profile root and runs the real generated _file_monitor_source via pwsh; asserts the log line splits to event in {Created,Changed} and field[2]==exact target path. Only works because the log path is delivered via -MessageData/$Event.MessageData; a $using: regression fails the action in the event runspace and produces no line.

Same runtime file-monitor gate plus test_renamed_file_event_records_old_and_new_path execute the real script against real Created and Renamed filesystem events and assert the exact pipe-delimited telemetry (new path in field[2], old path in field[3]); the action block can only emit these because MessageData carries the log path into the event runspace.

test_pid_automatic_variable_is_not_shadowed runs the real _process_monitor_source body once under Set-StrictMode/ErrorActionPreference=Stop, captures initial $PID, and throws if $PID changed; asserts returncode==0, 'Cannot overwrite variable PID' absent from stderr, and OK_PID_INTACT in stdout. test_spawned_process_lifecycle_is_logged additionally spawns a marked cmd.exe and asserts created|<pid>|cmd.exe then terminated lines, proving the $procId loop captures arbitrary PIDs.

pytestSummary: 30 passed in ~30s (22 passed transforms in 1.40s; 8 passed ps_sources in 28.92s)
